an4.6:1.1: “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of persons found existing in the world.
an4.6:1.3: One of little learning who is not intent on what he has learned;
an4.6:1.4: one of little learning who is intent on what he has learned;
an4.6:1.5: one of much learning who is not intent on what he has learned;
an4.6:1.6: and one of much learning who is intent on what he has learned.
an4.6:1.7: (1) “And how is a person one of little learning who is not intent on what he has learned?
an4.6:1.8: Here, someone has learned little—that is,
an4.6:1.9: of the discourses, mixed prose and verse, expositions, verses, inspired utterances, quotations, birth stories, amazing accounts, and questions-and-answers—
an4.6:1.10: but he does not understand the meaning of what he has learned; he does not understand the Dhamma; and he does not practice in accordance with the Dhamma. In such a way,
an4.6:1.11: a person is one of little learning who is not intent on what he has learned.
an4.6:2.1: (2) “And how is a person one of little learning who is intent on what he has learned?
an4.6:2.2: Here, someone has learned little—that is,
an4.6:2.4: but having understood the meaning of what he has learned, and having understood the Dhamma, he practices in accordance with the Dhamma. In such a way,
an4.6:2.5: a person is one of little learning who is intent on what he has learned.
an4.6:3.1: (3) “And how is a person one of much learning who is not intent on what he has learned?
an4.6:3.2: Here, someone has learned much—that is,
an4.6:3.4: but he does not understand the meaning of what he has learned; he does not understand the Dhamma; and he does not practice in accordance with the Dhamma. In such a way,
an4.6:3.5: a person is one of much learning who is not intent on what he has learned.
an4.6:4.1: (4) “And how is a person one of much learning who is intent on what he has learned?
an4.6:4.2: Here, someone has learned much—that is,
an4.6:4.4: and having understood the meaning of what he has learned, and having understood the Dhamma, he practices in accordance with the Dhamma. In such a way,
an4.6:4.5: a person is one of much learning who is intent on what he has learned.
an4.6:4.6: “These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of persons found existing in the world.”
an4.6:5.2: and is not settled in the virtues,
an4.6:5.3: they criticize him on both counts,
an4.6:6.2: but is well settled in the virtues,
an4.6:6.3: they praise him for his virtuous behavior;
an4.6:7.2: but is not settled in the virtues,
an4.6:7.3: they criticize him for his lack of virtue;
an4.6:8.2: and is settled in the virtues,
an4.6:8.3: they praise him on both counts,
an4.6:9.1: When a disciple of the Buddha is highly learned,
an4.6:9.2: an expert on the Dhamma, endowed with wisdom,
an4.6:9.3: like a coin of refined mountain gold,
an4.6:9.4: who is fit to blame him?
an4.6:9.5: Even the devas praise such a one;
an4.6:9.6: by Brahmā too he is praised.
